chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, from Ayub ibn Ayn, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, a man will be brought forth and it will be said to him: 'Present your argument.' He will say: 'O Lord, You created me and guided me, and You expanded sustenance upon me. I did not cease to expand upon Your creatures and make things easy for them, so that You would spread Your mercy upon me on this Day and make it easy for me.' So the Lord, Exalted is His Praise and High is His Mention, will say: 'My servant speaks the truth. Admit him into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the argument a believer presents on the Day of Judgment to enter Paradise based on their worldly conduct?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) conveys a unique intercessory argument where a servant justifies his entry into Paradise by citing his consistent generosity (*jawd*) and facilitation (*taysir*) for others as a means to invoke divine mercy. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on social benevolence not merely as charity, but as a spiritual mechanism that aligns the believer’s actions with God’s attribute of *Al-Wahhab* (The Bestower), thereby securing His favor on the Day of Judgment.
